BH-HF4-B1 — geometry and surface-field audit

Source: BH_HF4_birth_package.tar.gz.

First saved AH3: iteration 9536, t=18.625M. Previous selected frame 9504, t=18.5625M, has no AH3.

The triangle-area-weighted coordinate separation of AH1/AH2 centres is 1.163437M. This refines the earlier 1.1288M vertex-average estimate: the VTK grid is nonuniformly parameterised. These weights describe coordinate geometry, not physical horizon area.

First-AH3 coordinate spans are x=1.932784M, y=0.893932M, z=0.739868M, max/min=2.612335. Its area-weighted principal axis lies 4.544° from the AH1–AH2 line. Thus this coordinate representation is strongly elongated almost along the binary axis. By τ=0.3125M, span ratio falls to 2.316833.

τ / M Span ratio Re(Psi2) standard deviation Im(Psi2) standard deviation
1.7500 1.627833 0.479692 0.346215
1.8125 1.607518 0.473936 0.347446
1.9375 1.568002 0.463414 0.349789

No large coordinate-shape jump appears in the old spin/current-transition window. Sizes/dispersions vary smoothly, consistent with R2D: a strong J3/J5/J7 event need not involve a large separate surface deformation.

The local basis has u from AH1 to AH2, v transverse in the orbital plane, and w normal to that plane. The strongest Re(Psi2) deviation from its median is near a long-axis end, u_norm≈−0.973. Im(Psi2) peaks near a normal pole, w_norm≈−0.903. NP sigma has similar polar organisation. This is multipolar morphology, not one unique spot.

AH3 is an apparent horizon on a chosen slice, not a global event horizon. Cartesian sizes are coordinate-dependent; NP components depend on tetrad/gauge. Euclidean triangle area is not physical area. No physical identity with HF1 in another simulation is established.
